best_section.where: the gravel car park off Sir Samuel Griffith Drive, about 30 m downhill/east of the dropped pin, where the bush opens onto parking bays

drivers.seclusion: A forest trailhead/lookout car park backing onto dense Mt Coot-tha bushland, but it's a known day-use spot that pulls casual visitors and sits right on a scenic drive.
drivers.access_and_room: Formed gravel car park with multiple marked bays, reached directly off the road; plenty of room to pull off and park a van clear of traffic.
drivers.traffic: Sir Samuel Griffith Drive is a scenic one-way loop through the forest reserve; it carries sightseeing and commuter traffic, including at night, past the car park entrance.
drivers.convention: The 2022 QLD imagery shows well over a dozen cars using the lot, so vehicles parking there is clearly normal, though mostly for daytime bushwalking/lookout visits rather than overnight stays.

flags: Steep terrain near the pin itself (mean grade 16%, up to ~38%), though the car park area is close to flat
Day-use trailhead/lookout car park — likely to see casual visitors arriving even in the evening
Through traffic on a scenic drive past the car park entrance, including after dark
Can't tell from imagery whether the car park has a locking gate or night closure
reasons: Formed car park, not the overgrown pin site
Backs onto Mt Coot-tha forest reserve
Popular day-use lot sees passing visitors
rubbish: None seen in the car park or surrounding bush.
summary: A forested lookout car park off a scenic drive — secluded by night but a known day-use spot with passing traffic.
sun_shade: Eucalypt canopy shades the car park from the west (bush side); the road-facing east edge is more open to the sky.
cannot_judge: Whether the car park has a gate or is closed/locked overnight
